# Alexander K Saeri

> Alexander K Saeri directs the MIT AI Risk Initiative at MIT FutureTech. He conducts and communicates research to help govern highly capable general-purpose AI, and holds positions at MIT FutureTech and The University of Queensland. He is based in Melbourne, Australia.

His methods background is in social psychology, applied behaviour science, implementation science, evidence synthesis, systems thinking, and survey research. Alongside the MIT AI Risk Initiative, he helps build Australia's AI safety ecosystem: he advises AI safety organisations in Australia, co-founded the Melbourne AI Safety Hub (https://maish.au/) coworking space, convenes the AI Safety Unconference (https://aisum.org/; 2023, 2025 and 2026), designed and facilitated the inaugural Australian AI Safety Forum (https://aisafetyforum.au/) in 2024, and spoke at the 2026 Forum.

## MIT AI Risk Initiative

- [airisk.mit.edu](https://airisk.mit.edu/): the Initiative's home
- [AI Risk Repository](https://airisk.mit.edu/risks): what are the risks from AI?
- [AI Risk Priorities](https://airisk.mit.edu/priorities): which risks matter most?
- [AI Incident Tracker](https://airisk.mit.edu/ai-incident-tracker): where is AI already causing harm?
- [AI Risk Disclosure Tracker](https://airisk.mit.edu/company-disclosures): how are the world's largest companies responding?
- [AI Risk Mitigation Repository](https://airisk.mit.edu/ai-risk-mitigations): what can reduce the risks?
- [AI Governance Map](https://airisk.mit.edu/ai-governance): how is AI being governed?

## Selected publications

- [Unmitigated? How are the world's largest companies responding to AI risks?](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2611.04278) (2026, arXiv; first author)
- [The AI Risk Mitigation Repository: A systematic review and multi-taxonomy framework of mitigations across AI systems, organizations, and ecosystems](https://airisk.mit.edu/mitigations) (2026, MIT AI Risk Initiative; joint first author)
- [Assessing Company Contributions to Societal Resilience: Extending the Societal Capacity Assessment Framework to Agentic AI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.27238) (2026, arXiv)
- [Prioritization of Risks from Artificial Intelligence: A Delphi Study of 272 International Experts](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2606.04490) (2026, arXiv; first author)
- [The AI Risk Repository: A meta-review, database, and taxonomy of risks from artificial intelligence](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patter.2026.101517) (2026, Patterns)
- [Affordance Analyses of AI Safety Policies: A Proof-of-Concept using OpenAI's Preparedness Framework](https://doi.org/10.1145/3805689.3812331) (2026, ACM FAccT)
- [Strategic insights from simulation gaming of AI race dynamics](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.futures.2025.103563) (2025, Futures)
- [Survey Assessing Risks from Artificial Intelligence: Technical Report](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4750953) (2024; first author), followed by the [2025 Technical Report](https://aigovernance.org.au/survey/2025/)
